newsitem.title: USA: Iron Mountain sees growth above targets.
newsitem.headline: Iron Mountain sees growth above targets.

text.p: Iron Mountain Inc said Thursday it expected revenue and operating income growth to be "significantly above" its targets in the next quarters, despite reporting a net loss for the quarter ended June 30.
The data storage company posted a net loss of $969,000, or $0.09 a share, in the quarter, compared with a $411,000 net profit, or $0.04 a share, last year.

The company said it expected a gain on the proceeds of its business interruption insurance for fires at its New Brunswick, N.J., facilities in March. It added the fires will not have a adverse effect on the company's results.

"Taking into account customary internal growth, the growth yet to be realized from completed acquisitions, and a strong acquisition pipeline, we anticipate operating at growth rates significantly above our targets for a number of quarters going forward", said chief executive Richard Reese in a statement.

The company's earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, amortization and extraordinary charges, increased 40.7 percent to $11.2 million in the quarter, from $7.9 million a year ago. Revenues rose 41.5 percent to $46.6 million from $32.9 million over the same period.
The company attributed most of the growth to the operations of its recent acquisitions, 12 companies, in the first half of this year.
Iron Mountain's interest expense ballooned to $1 million in the quarter, compared with an interest income of $934,000 last year.
